Fixed in b33dc598d: the bind cleanup now bumps the bind generation before it detaches, so a `plugin_ui_get` still pending when the pane unmounts never attaches the chat it left. A one-key Send that was already made still reaches that chat.

Fixed in 512ae52ee. `invoke` now always returns the plugin's verdict and only gates the reducer dispatch on the bind generation, so a refused one-key Send sends nothing even after the pane unmounts or the transport reconnects. `use` checks that the pane is still on the same chat, so a Use refusal after a same-chat reconnect still empties the box, while one after a switch to another chat leaves it alone. Tests cover the unmount, reconnect and session-switch cases.

Thanks — the mechanism is right (the bootstrap drops `ctx.ui.update` once `disposing` is set, so the rule set served in `NextSession.dispose()` never reaches a slot on idle reclaim), but we're leaving this as is:

- **The fallback isn't for the tray.** It exists so a one-shot run on a host that renders no slot still records its offer. On desktop teardown the synthesized detach runs first, so `dispose()` serves nothing there.
- **The trigger needs an unrealistic setting.** The detached planner window is at most ~21 s (facts budget + the 20 s planner deadline); the idle default is 30 min (`DEFAULT_PLUGIN_SANDBOX_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`) and no host sets `CLINE_PLUGIN_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`. Below ~21 s every worker would also be reclaimed between hooks during ordinary model calls.
- **It matches the documented contract.** Idle eviction only waits on in-flight RPCs and plugin state is ephemeral across eviction (ARCHITECTURE.md, the plugins README's sandboxed-lifetime section); Next Turn persists the served set for exactly this.
- **It heals on the next RPC, not only on reopen.** The next message runs `beforeModel`, whose `outgoing()` turns the tray off, and a re-attach serves the restored set.

Dropping cleanup UI updates is deliberate, so a reclaimed worker's teardown can never overwrite a live session's tray.

Fixed in 0b6e96f80b. `use` and `send` reply `ok` only when the set currently shown has that revision and still lists that item id; otherwise they're refused as stale (before the first set, after a later turn or refresh, after a row was skipped, or while hidden). After a worker restart, setup now withdraws the set core still holds, so the tray never shows rows the fresh worker would refuse.

Fixed in f83618bd27. `begin()` now only stages the new epoch. `activate()` promotes it once the replacement session is resident. Until then the resident session keeps its slot state, viewers and UI chain, and keeps serving invokes. A start that fails releases only its staged epoch, so a failed reopen leaves the working chat's suggestions as they were. `clearPlugin` also takes the epoch now, so a plugin that fails while the replacement is starting can't clear the resident copy.

Covered by "serves the resident session while a same-id start is pending and after it fails" in `local-runtime-host.plugin-ui.test.ts`, plus the staging cases in `store.test.ts` and `service.teardown.test.ts`.

Fixed in 8aa28b7877. The page no longer decides from its own busy flag, which can lag behind the Hub. The sidecar applies the Hub's statuses and slot states in order. It now records each chat's latest slot order and snapshots it when a turn starts running. `plugin_ui_get` replies with the states, whether a turn is under way and, when the sidecar saw the turn start, the slot orders at that start.

The page marks a fetched set as from before the turn only when the set is no newer than that start. A set `afterRun` just published is therefore kept, whether the Hub had already reported idle or was still persisting the turn. For a turn the sidecar didn't see start, it falls back to the old behavior. The tracking also survives a sidebar re-attach.

Covered in `use-composer-suggestions.test.tsx`: "keeps a set the Hub published as the turn ended, while the page still showed the chat running" and the "keeps a set the running turn published before the bind" cases. The sidecar tracking is covered in `plugin-ui.test.ts` and `chat-session.test.ts`.

Right: sharing the shutdown steps had moved the abort behind `shutdownSession`'s git-metadata and status-write awaits for the `dispose`/`delete`/failure paths (`stopSession` aborts before calling in, so it was unaffected). Folded into "share the teardown steps between shutdownSession and releaseSessionRuntime": the abort now lives in `beginTeardown`, which runs synchronously before teardown's first await, so `aborting` is set before the team continuation loop or any tool call can observe the session mid-teardown; `shutDownSessionRuntime` keeps the plugin-tail wait and the agent/runtime/sandbox shutdown. New test disposes a session mid-run and asserts `agent.abort` is called before the `cancelled` status write is issued; moving the abort back fails it.

fixed in e68bb30086.

The hub now remembers every app that registered each callback for a task, including an app that joins a task while it's running. Each callback request goes to the original app while it's connected. If that app is gone, the request goes to the next connected app that registered the same callback. So when the original app closes, the app that joined takes over the callbacks, and sending another message works.

Tests:
- New hub test: once the owner unregisters, the request goes to the joined client.
- End-to-end run: after the original app left, the task kept running for 5 more steps with the joined app answering.

What's left: if no connected app registered that callback (for example, the joining app never registers it), the request still fails right away with the "disconnected… send a message to continue" message. Desktop re-creates the task on its next send once the run has ended, which builds fresh callbacks, so that message is accurate there.

Agreed, fixed in 34056fc61. After waiting for Hub startup, `handleCommand` now rejects the command if its connection is no longer in `ctx.wsClients`. The close handler has already run by then, so nothing else could cancel work started for that connection. Covered by `drops a waiting command whose connection closed during startup` in `commands-hub-startup.test.ts`.

Valid, and it contradicts the comment a few lines above ("Once spawned, keep the shared startup lock until discovery is published. Cancelling a waiter must not let another waiter launch a duplicate daemon"). At `815be409c` the post-spawn probes had no signal; now both `probeHubForStartup` calls in the loop receive `signal`, so an abort throws an `AbortError` that the `catch` does not swallow, and the lock is released while the daemon is still booting. Impact is bounded by the OS-level `HubInstanceLock` (a duplicate daemon loses the singleton race), so low severity, but the fix is just dropping `signal` from those two calls; `deadline` already bounds them.

+		if (this.scopeTransition || this.disposed) return

+			return

+				// example from the dashboard). Close its connection rather than keep
+				// it in History; the task on screen keeps its host so that opening it
+				// can explain the deletion (see explainConnectFailure).
+				for (const [id, entry] of this.entries) {
+					if (seen.has(id) || this.isHostInUse(entry)) continue
+					this.entries.delete(id)
+					this.statusResolutionAttempts.delete(id)
+					void entry.host?.dispose("deleted").catch(() => undefined)
+				}

+			} catch (error) {

+				if (generation !== this.scopeGeneration || this.disposed) return

+					// the retained connections that nothing is using. The displayed task
+					// keeps its entry and host: closing them would leave a task on screen
+					// that cannot continue even after the user signs in again, and its
+					// next interaction reports the authentication failure itself.
+					for (const [id, entry] of this.entries) {

+					}

+				Logger.warn("[CloudSessions] Failed to refresh cloud session list:", error)

+			} finally {
+				if (this.listPromise === listPromise) {

+				}
+			}
+		})()

+	private upsertRecord(record: CloudSessionRecord): CloudSessionEntry {

+			// settled outcomes against the record just as we do after restart.

+	private handleStatusChange(sessionId: string, status: CloudSessionStatus): void {

+	private upsertRecord(record: CloudSessionRecord): CloudSessionEntry {

+			// settled outcomes against the record just as we do after restart.
+			if (existing.agentStatus && isSettled(existing.agentStatus)) {
+				existing.agentStatus = this.rememberedStatusOf(record)
+			}
+			return existing
+		}
+		const entry: CloudSessionEntry = {
+			record,
+			pinned: 0,
+			agentStatus: this.rememberedStatusOf(record),
+			lastActivityAt: Date.parse(record.updatedAt) || Date.now(),
+		}

+		return entry
+	}

+	/** Changes account scope as one boundary: invalidate, detach, dispose, mutate scope, then reopen reads. */
+	async reset(changeScope?: () => Promise<void>): Promise<void> {

+		// so the drain below waits for its DELETE, not for the sandbox to boot.
+		this.cancelPendingStart()

+		this.statusResolutionAttempts.clear()

+		const transition = (async () => {
+			await previousTransition

+			}

+				await this.options.clearTask()
+			}

+			const hosts = entries.flatMap((entry) => (entry.host ? [entry.host] : []))
+			const connections = entries.flatMap((entry) => (entry.connection ? [entry.connection] : []))

+			// account active through every await, including DELETE; never retain old tokens.

+		})()

+			await transition

+				// before a later auth/config refresh failed.

+	}

+	private trackScopeOperation<T>(operation: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
+		// Enroll before executing any code that can yield or re-enter reset.
+		const promise = Promise.resolve().then(operation)
+		this.scopeOperations.add(promise)
+		return promise.finally(() => this.scopeOperations.delete(promise))

+	private async drainScopeOperations(operations: Promise<unknown>[]): Promise<void> {
+		let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined

+			await Promise.race([
+				Promise.allSettled(operations),
+				new Promise<never>((_resolve, reject) => {
+					timer = setTimeout(
+						() =>
+							reject(
+								new Error(
+									"Cloud session cleanup is still pending. Your account has not changed; try again after cleanup finishes.",
+								),
+							),
+						SCOPE_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS,
+					)
+				}),
+			])
+		} finally {
+			clearTimeout(timer)
+		}
+	}

+	private async connect(entry: CloudSessionEntry): Promise<CloudSessionHost> {
+		if (entry.connection) {
+			return entry.connection

+		const taskId = entry.record.metadata.taskId?.trim()
+		if (!taskId) {
+			throw new Error(`Cloud session ${sessionId} has no canonical task id.`)
+		}
+		const generation = this.scopeGeneration
+		const record = entry.record
+		const connection = (async () => {
+			const retainedHost = entry.host
+			const host =
+				retainedHost ??
+				(await CloudSessionHost.connect({
+					outerSessionId: sessionId,
+					taskId,
+					sandboxType: record.sandboxType ?? record.metadata.sandboxType,
+					socketUrl: this.options.cloudSessions.sessionSocketUrl(sessionId),
+					getAuthToken: this.options.getAuthToken,
+					requestToolApproval: this.options.requestToolApproval,
+					telemetry: this.options.telemetry,
+					restoreConfig: () => this.cloudSessionConfig(record.metadata.modelId ?? this.nextCloudModelId()),
+					onStatusChange: (status) => {
+						// A replaced account entry must never receive its predecessor's events.
+						if (!this.disposed && generation === this.scopeGeneration && this.entries.get(sessionId) === entry) {
+							this.handleStatusChange(sessionId, status)
+						}
+					},
+				}))
+			const status = retainedHost ? await retainedHost.refreshStatus() : host.status
+			if (this.disposed || generation !== this.scopeGeneration || this.entries.get(sessionId) !== entry) {
+				await host.dispose("accountScopeChanged").catch(() => undefined)
+				throw new Error("Cloud session connection was superseded")
+			}
+			entry.host = host
+			// A later list may invalidate the snapshot while the RPC is pending.
+			if (entry.record === record) {
+				entry.agentStatus = status
+				if (isSettled(status)) this.rememberStatus(record, status, Date.now())
+				else if (ACTIVE_CLOUD_STATUSES.has(status)) this.forgetStatus(record.id)
+			}
+			this.ensurePolling()
+			return host
+		})()
+		entry.connection = connection
+		try {
+			return await connection
+		} finally {
+			if (entry.connection === connection) entry.connection = undefined
+		}
+	}
+
+	private handleStatusChange(sessionId: string, status: CloudSessionStatus): void {
+		const entry = this.entries.get(sessionId)
+		if (!entry) {
+			return
+		}
+		const previous = entry.agentStatus
+		const now = Date.now()
+		entry.agentStatus = status
+		if (isSettled(status)) {
+			this.rememberStatus(entry.record, status, now)
+		} else if (ACTIVE_CLOUD_STATUSES.has(status)) {
+			this.forgetStatus(entry.record.id)
+		}
+		// Learning the current status on connect is not agent activity; only a
+		// change observed while connected moves the task up in History.
+		if (previous !== undefined && previous !== status) {
+			entry.lastActivityAt = now
+		}
+		this.options.invalidateHistoryCache()
+		const isDisplayed = this.options.getTask()?.taskId === sessionId
+		if (!isDisplayed && previous !== undefined && previous !== status && (status === "completed" || status === "failed")) {
+			this.notifyFinished(entry, status)
+		}
+		this.options.postStateToWebview().catch(() => {})
+	}
+
+	private notifyFinished(entry: CloudSessionEntry, status: CloudSessionStatus): void {
+		const title = entry.record.title?.trim() || entry.title || entry.record.repoContext.repoUrl || entry.record.id
+		const label = status === "failed" ? "Cloud task failed" : "Cloud task finished"
+		HostProvider.window
+			.showMessage({
+				type: status === "failed" ? ShowMessageType.WARNING : ShowMessageType.INFORMATION,
+				message: `${label}: ${title}`,
+				options: { items: ["Open"] },
+			})
+			.then((response) => {
+				if (!this.disposed && this.entries.get(entry.record.id) === entry && response.selectedOption === "Open") {
+					return this.openCloudTask(entry.record.id)
+				}
+				return undefined
+			})
+			.catch((error) => Logger.warn("[CloudSessions] Failed to show completion notification:", error))
+	}

+	private ensurePolling(): void {
+		if (this.pollTimer || this.disposed) {
+			return
+		}
+		this.pollTimer = setInterval(() => void this.pollTick(), ACTIVE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS)

+	}

+	private async pollTick(): Promise<void> {
+		if (this.disposed) {
+			return
+		}

+			const status = this.statusOf(entry)
+			if (
+				entry.host &&
+				!this.isHostInUse(entry) &&
+				!ACTIVE_CLOUD_STATUSES.has(status) &&
+				// Loss of observation is not evidence that the sandbox stopped.
+				status !== "unknown" &&
+				now - entry.lastActivityAt > IDLE_CONNECTION_TTL_MS
+			) {
+				// Finished a while ago and nobody is looking: release the socket.
+				await entry.host.dispose("idle").catch(() => undefined)
+				entry.host = undefined
+			}
+		}
+		const hasActive = [...this.entries.values()].some((entry) => ACTIVE_CLOUD_STATUSES.has(this.statusOf(entry)))

+			await this.refreshList(true)
+			this.options.invalidateHistoryCache()
+			this.options.postStateToWebview().catch(() => {})
+		}
+		if (![...this.entries.values()].some((entry) => entry.host)) {
+			clearInterval(this.pollTimer)
+			this.pollTimer = undefined
+		}
+	}

+	/**
+	 * The Cline model a new sandbox runs: the user's Act-mode Cline model,

+			return apiConfig.actModeClineModelId.trim()

+	/**

+				}
+			})
+			.catch(() => undefined)
+			.finally(() => {
+				if (this.recommendedModelsWarmup === warmup) {

+	/** The model the displayed cloud task runs on, else the one a new cloud task would use. */
+	getCloudModelId(): string {

+	/**
+	 * Claims the next cloud start synchronously and returns the function that
+	 * runs it. Callers that must await other work first (remote config) claim
+	 * before awaiting, so a Cancel arriving in that gap invalidates this start.
+	 */
+	beginCloudTask(input: CloudTaskInput): () => Promise<string | undefined> {

+		this.pendingStartTask = undefined

+		// showing when the user submitted.
+		const modelId = this.nextCloudModelId()
+		return async () => {
+			try {
+				await this.scopeTransition
+				if (
+					this.disposed ||
+					generationBeforeTransition !== this.scopeGeneration ||
+					startGeneration !== this.startGeneration

+					return undefined

+					this.startCloudTaskInScope(input, modelId, generationBeforeTransition, startGeneration, pendingStart.signal),

+					this.pendingStartTask = undefined
+					this.renewPendingStartView = undefined

+					this.options.invalidateHistoryCache()

+					// re-post so the composer no longer sees "provisioning".
+					this.options.postStateToWebview().catch(() => {})

+			}
+		}
+	}

+	/**

+	 * stops the readiness poll, so the sandbox record is deleted as soon as the
+	 * control plane answers instead of after the sandbox finishes starting.

+	cancelPendingStart(): boolean {
+		const pendingStart = this.pendingStart
+		if (!pendingStart) {
+			return false
+		}

+		this.pendingStartSessionId = undefined
+		this.pendingStartTask = undefined
+		this.renewPendingStartView = undefined

+	/**

+	 */

+	/** The sandbox session config a start uses, and that a resumed sandbox rebuilds its conversation with. */

+			knownModels: _knownModels,

+			// (the Cline provider key) must never be shipped into it. It resolves

+	private async startCloudTaskInScope(
+		input: CloudTaskInput,
+		modelId: string,
+		generation: number,
+		startGeneration: number,
+		cancelSignal: AbortSignal,
+	): Promise<string | undefined> {
+		if (this.disposed || generation !== this.scopeGeneration || startGeneration !== this.startGeneration) return undefined
+		// Keep the claim clearTask made: claiming again after the await would
+		// override a selection the user made while the view was clearing.
+		let isSuperseded = await this.options.clearTask()
+		if (this.disposed || isSuperseded() || generation !== this.scopeGeneration || startGeneration !== this.startGeneration)
+			return undefined
+		let abandoned = false
+		const isStale = () => {
+			abandoned ||=
+				this.disposed || isSuperseded() || generation !== this.scopeGeneration || startGeneration !== this.startGeneration

+		}

+			if (abandoned) return false

+		const sandboxLabel = `${repoLabel}${input.branch ? ` (${input.branch})` : ""}`
+		const provisioningRow = (text: string): ClineMessage => ({
+			ts: startedAt + 1,
+			type: "say",
+			say: "text",

+			partial: false,

+					type: "say",
+					say: "task",
+					text: input.prompt,
+					...(input.images?.length ? { images: input.images } : {}),
+					partial: false,
+				},
+				provisioningRow(`Starting a cloud sandbox for ${sandboxLabel}…`),
+			],
+			provisioningEvent,
+		)
+		this.options.clearTurnOutcome()
+		this.options.setTurnPhase("streaming")
+		this.options.postStateToWebview().catch(() => {})

+		let sessionId: string | undefined
+		let entry: CloudSessionEntry | undefined
+		let host: SdkSessionHost | undefined
+		let sent = false
+		try {
+			const config = await this.cloudSessionConfig(modelId)

+			if (isStale()) return sessionId

+			if (isStale()) return sessionId

+				config: { ...config, sessionId: record.id },
+				interactive: true,

+			// Throws if the record cannot be dropped; the start then fails and deletes the sandbox.
+			this.journal?.remove(record.id)

+				[

+						ts: Date.now(),

+						say: "error",
+						text: `Failed to start the cloud session: ${detail}`,

+		} finally {

+	private async cleanupUnusedSession(sessionId: string, entry?: CloudSessionEntry, host?: SdkSessionHost): Promise<void> {

+		// held an entry for it (a cancelled create never reaches upsertRecord), so
+		// drop whatever entry carries this id unless a successor replaced it.
+		const listed = this.entries.get(sessionId)

+			await this.options.sessions.endActiveSessionIfHost(host, "cloudStartSuperseded").catch(() => {
+				failed = true

+				failed = true
+			})
+		}

+			() => this.forgetPendingStart(sessionId),
+			(error: unknown) => {
+				if (error instanceof CloudSessionError && error.code === "session_not_found") {
+					this.forgetPendingStart(sessionId)
+					return
+				}
+				failed = true
+			},
+		)
+		// The pending start's own invalidation is skipped when it was cancelled,
+		// so History learns here that the record is gone.
+		this.options.invalidateHistoryCache()
+		this.options.postStateToWebview().catch(() => {})

+			const message =
+				"Cloud sandbox cleanup could not be confirmed. Open History in the account that started it and delete the unused cloud session."
+			Logger.warn(`[CloudSessions] ${message}`)
+			void HostProvider.window.showMessage({ type: ShowMessageType.WARNING, message }).catch(() => {

+			})
+		}
+	}

+	// ---- Reopening a task from History ----

discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed. The record is now forgotten only when `CloudSessionHost.whenTurnAccepted()` resolves, i.e. when the Hub reports run activity for the session or `runTurn` returns, not when the send is launched. If a host exits after acceptance but before forgetting, recovery inspects the sandbox and leaves it if it has taken a turn. Covered by `keeps a provisioning sandbox recorded until the sandbox accepts its first turn`.

Fair, fixed in 1ffebc669. It now mirrors a live session, where abort stops the running turn and leaves queued prompts: the pending-start entry counts waiters in arrival order and an abort cancels only the earliest one (the turn that would have been running); later waiters run on the replacement. Test extended with a second waiting turn that completes while the first is aborted.

`request()` coalesces a newer request into `pending`, but it doesn't invalidate an already-active rebuild for the same reason — `cancellationGeneration` only moves in `cancel()` (line 40). So the active run's `isCurrent()` stays `true`, and once it finishes the newer request rebuilds the session again.

There's a correctness window here, not just redundant work. If the active rebuild has already snapshotted its config when the newer setting arrives, it installs the superseded one; and for checkpoint rebuilds it can replay a deferred follow-up from the shared `checkpointTransition` before the newer rebuild applies the latest setting — so a real message can run under the old checkpoint config.

I don't think bumping the generation here is a self-contained fix: the transition object is shared between the active and queued requests, and an invalidated rebuild returning from `replaceActiveSession()` can still clear `this.checkpointTransition` and stop the replacement. Either make a same-reason request explicitly supersede the active run with the transition ownership handled to match, or rename `isCurrent()` so it's clear it only means "not cancelled". A scheduler test for requesting a reason while that reason is actively rebuilding would pin whichever contract you pick.

Thanks — you were right on both counts, and the second one hid a real defect.

`isCurrent()` in a78223a means exactly "no newer request for the same reason has arrived": `request()` stamps a per-reason generation, and a running rebuild's context reads it live. `cancel()` and the per-reason cancellation generation are gone; nothing could reach them because `runTaskTransition` waits for the drain first.

The shared `checkpointTransition` is gone too. Holding a follow-up outside Core's queue meant nothing rendered it: a message typed during a turn after toggling Checkpoints vanished from the chat until the turn ended (this is what the e2e was failing on across all three CI platforms). Follow-ups now always go to Core's queue. The scheduler treats a session with queued prompts as busy, since Core drains the queue the instant a turn ends, and a send that settles after Core already started the next queued turn no longer flips the session idle. There is a scheduler test for a same-reason request during an active rebuild, and coordinator tests for supersession before replacement.

`waitUntilSettled` has no production caller left — this PR removes the one that existed (`await this.sessionRebuilds.waitUntilSettled()` in `SdkController`), and the send path now goes through `handlePendingRebuilds`, which parks the follow-up and returns `"deferred"` rather than awaiting. Only the scheduler's own tests reference it now. Worth dropping unless a caller is coming: a test-only affordance on a production class tends to acquire one later without the concurrency implications getting re-examined.

Dropped in b3cb45d, along with `hasPendingRebuild` and the settled-waiter list. The follow-up path no longer awaits the scheduler at all; a running-turn follow-up goes straight to Core's queue and the rebuild waits for the queue to drain.
